question: Cl on Rs. 2000 for 1 year at 10% p.a. is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 1 year, Compound Interest = Simple Interest

CI = P × R × T ÷ 100

= 2000 × 10 × 1 ÷ 100

= ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Principal = ₹2000

Rate = 10% p.a.

Time = 1 year

Formula Used:

Amount = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T

CI = Amount − Principal

 
• Start 1 Year P = ₹2000 Rate = 10% CI after 1 year 

⇒ Amount = 2000(1 + 10 ÷ 100)¹

⇒ = 2000 × 110 ÷ 100

⇒ = ₹2200

⇒ CI = 2200 − 2000

⇒ CI = ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100 where P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time.

Compound Interest Formula

Amount = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T and CI = Amount − Principal.

SI and CI Relation

For 1 year, Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always equal.

Rule of 72

Approximate doubling time = 72 ÷ Rate%.
